messages:
maria: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-payments) reporting 401s starting ~10:15 UTC after we rotated their API key. They say the SDK still uses old key in prod, intermittent 401s. Can someone help triage?

alex: Checking. Do we have request IDs or example timestamps from the customer? Any recent deploys?

maria: They sent sample logs: `req_id=87c2a2b, 2026-03-15T10:18:03Z, status=401, error=invalid_api_key`. No user-facing deploys in last 24h. They said they used Helm to deploy their service and rotate keys via CI that writes k8s secrets from pipeline.

ryan: Quick suspicion: Helm/CI might've updated a k8s Secret named `acme-api-key` but the Deployment mounts it as env and the pods didn't restart, so old value remained in memory. Also some apps read from a mounted file and only reload on SIGHUP. Do we know how their app consumes the secret?

maria: Customer confirms their app reads env var ACME_API_KEY at startup (not watching file). Their pipeline does `kubectl create secret generic acme-api-key --from-literal=key=$NEW_KEY --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`. They said helm values also have `apiKey: <redacted>` which they didn't update.

alex: That `helm values` bit is suspicious — if their helm chart templated a Secret with the same name and they re-applied chart without bumping chart release, helm's computed manifest might have re-created the old secret (chart value wins). Can you paste their `kubectl get secret acme-api-key -o go-template='{{index .data "key"}}' | base64 -d` output (redact actual key) and `kubectl get deploy -o yaml` for annotations?

maria: I asked customer to run those. They pasted `echo xxxxx` (redacted). Looks like the cluster secret value is the new key. But pod env shows old key in stack traces: `env ACME_API_KEY=sk_oldkey...`. Pod age is 3d.

ryan: So pods didn't restart after secret changed. That's expected — k8s doesn't auto-restart pods when a Secret value changes. If their CI applied the secret only (not rolling restart), the existing pods continue using the in-memory env. Fix options: 1) trigger a rollout restart: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/acme-service -n prod` 2) update an env var annotation to force new pod template 3) patch the deployment with an annotation `kubectl patch deploy acme-service -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rotated":"$(date +%s)"}}}}}'`.

maria: Customer did `kubectl apply -f secret.yaml` but not a rollout. They asked if we can revoke the old key to force failures so they can detect sooner.

alex: We can revoke the old key, but that will cause 100% failures until pods restart. Better to coordinate: we advise them to restart pods after CI rotates secret, or update CI to call `kubectl rollout restart` post-secret-update. For immediate mitigation, do a rolling restart so new pods pick up the secret.

vaultbot: Vault: apikey `apc-12345` revoked at 2026-03-15T10:20:45Z by maria.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3197 — 401s after apikey rotation (owner: support).

ryan: If their helm chart contains a `values.yaml` with `apiKey` field, recommend removing plaintext values and sourcing from external secret store (Vault/KMS). Also show recommended pattern: 1) CI writes secret to Vault 2) CI updates k8s Secret and then `kubectl rollout restart` OR 3) use Vault Agent sidecar with k8s auth so pods fetch secrets at start and support token renewal.

maria: Customer accepted rolling restart. Ran `kubectl rollout restart deployment/acme-service -n prod` — new pods came up, logs show auth success. They asked for a prevention checklist. I drafted steps below.

alex: Nice. Can you paste the checklist in the thread? We should keep a short support KB.

maria: Checklist copied for KB:
- Use Vault/KMS as source of truth; avoid committing keys into Helm values.
- CI rotation flow: write new secret to Vault -> update k8s Secret -> `kubectl rollout restart deployment/<svc>` (or patch pod template).
- If using file-mounted secrets or sidecars, ensure the app reloads config or use readiness probe gating on secret refresh.
- For immediate revocation workflows, coordinate a maintenance window; revoking before pods pick up new key causes 401s.
- For Helm-managed secrets, bump chart release or update values and `helm upgrade` so chart doesn't overwrite manual secret updates.

ryan: Add small kubectl commands for KB: `kubectl get secret acme-api-key -n prod -o jsonpath='{.data.key}' | base64 -d` and `kubectl rollout status deploy/acme-service -n prod`.

maria: I'll open a KB article and link this thread. Closing ticket once customer confirms stability. :white_check_mark:
